text:
maya: Quick thread — thinking through token eviction semantics for the credits pipeline. TL;DR: we need a small, deterministic contract for when a token is considered evaporated vs late-arrival recoverable.
samir: +1. Are we talking about the provisional token that the runtime emits, or the compacted ledger token after joiners?
nora: Both. Runtime provisional tokens show up fast but sometimes miss provenance. Compact ledger might see them later. We should avoid double-charging when the late one lands.
liam: Proposed idea: mark provisional tokens with an epoch+nonce header, keep a 5m soft-window for reconciliation, then tombstone provisional entries and credit from compact path.
maya: 5m seems OK for most, but enterprise customers with strict accounting want deterministic cutoffs. Maybe expose a per-tenant retention/eviction param?
ops-carol: We already have per-tenant grace for quota enforcement; exposing a billing-level grace makes sense but adds rollout complexity. Also need to surface in invoices.
samir: Tradeoff: per-tenant param -> complexity + more storage. Global default + tenant override for enterprise seems reasonable.
liam: Implementation sketch: augment token envelope with provenance pointer and "evict-after" timestamp. Ingest service keeps provisional until evict-after, reconciler can absorb late arrivals if seq < evict-after.
nora: What about replays and dedupe? We need idempotency keys across both provisional and compact paths. Otherwise reconciler can't tell if compact event already accounted for.
maya: Agree. Use combined key: tenant|fingerprint|provenance-source|event-seq. Keep it as the canonical dedupe key.
infra-bot: note: reconciler job "credits-recon-v2" scheduled every 2m. Might need tune if we extend soft windows.
liam: Also need an audit trail: when we tombstone provisional token, emit an audit event with reason=evicted and pointer to claim id. That way finance can trace.
ops-carol: Can we compress audit retention? Long tail audits blow up S3 costs. Maybe policy: keep detailed audit 90d, aggregated ballot 2y.
samir: Sounds fine, but we must keep raw proofs for compliance customers longer — tie to tenant SLA flag.
nora: Backfill story: if we change the evict-after semantics, backfills could retroactively mark tokens. We should avoid rewriting historical invoices. Instead, write reconciliation markers and only apply to future windows.
maya: Exactly. No retroactive billing changes without manual review. Reconciler writes an "adjustment candidate" stream for ops to approve.
liam: Another edge: prefix-caching at runtime can hide token splits (same logical request split across sub-requests). Need to stitch at ingestion so attribution stays correct. Prefer: runtime emits parent_id in envelope. Ingest uses parent_id to join shards.
samir: Parent_id helps but increases cardinality for dedupe. We should only include parent_id for split requests, keep default absent.
ora: For metrics: we need per-route, per-model, per-tenant charge breakdowns. That ties back to envelope schema — include route/model tags.
maya: Good point — include model_id, route_name, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens. Keep fields minimal to avoid huge schema churn.
liam: Security note: provenance pointers may leak internal IDs. Mask before sending to tenants in audit UI. Internal audit retains full pointer.
ora: Ops: what about emergency rollback if we find a bad reconciliation rule? We need a revert path that creates negative adjustments not to touch original ledger.
ops-carol: We already have adjustments pipeline that appends corrective entries. Use that. Ops needs a UI to approve candidate adjustments from recon job.
maya: Action items: 1) Samir to draft envelope schema w/ evict-after + parent_id + model/route tags. 2) Liam to spike reconciler idempotency key logic and tombstone audit events. 3) Nora to write backfill/adjustment policy doc. 4) Ops-Carol to spec admin approval UI.
samir: I'll put schema draft in a PR by EOD tomorrow.
liam: I'll prototype dedupe in the sandbox pipeline this week.
ora: I'll start the policy doc draft — flagging potential billing/legal review.
ops-carol: I'll sketch the UI flows, low-fi first.
maya: Thanks all. If anyone sees failure modes I missed — drop them here.
liam: One more: consider a compact-merge window where compact events older than X are treated as canonical and provisional are ignored. X should be tunable per-tenant.
maya: Noted. We'll add that param to the schema proposal.
ora: Also, put a note about alerts: spikes in "evicted" audit events should page eng-platform. Could indicate runtime regression.
infra-bot: alert created: "evicted-audit-spike" -> paging rule set to eng-platform on >100/min spike.
maya: Perfect. Closing for now — thanks. :thumbsup:
